question_text: A 59-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe pain (10/10 in severity) between the shoulder blades. He describes the pain as tearing in nature. Medical history is positive for essential hypertension for 11 years. The patient has smoked 10–15 cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. His temperature is 36.6°C (97.8°F), the heart rate is 107/min, and the blood pressure is 179/86 mm Hg in the right arm and 157/72 mm Hg in the left arm. CT scan of the chest shows an intimal flap limited to the descending thoracic aorta. Which of the following best describes the most likely predisposing factor for this condition?

                    ### Question
                    A 59-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe pain (10/10 in severity) between the shoulder blades. He describes the pain as tearing in nature. Medical history is positive for essential hypertension for 11 years. The patient has smoked 10–15 cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. His temperature is 36.6°C (97.8°F), the heart rate is 107/min, and the blood pressure is 179/86 mm Hg in the right arm and 157/72 mm Hg in the left arm. CT scan of the chest shows an intimal flap limited to the descending thoracic aorta. Which of the following best describes the most likely predisposing factor for this condition?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with severe tearing pain and has a CT scan showing an intimal flap in the descending thoracic aorta, indicative of aortic dissection. Long-standing essential hypertension is a well-known risk factor for aortic dissection, as it can lead to structural changes in the aorta, including abnormal elastic properties. Smoking further exacerbates cardiovascular risk, but the primary predisposing factor in this case is the hypertension, which contributes to arterial stiffness and changes in the aortic wall. Therefore, the most likely predisposing factor for this condition is abnormal elastic properties of the aorta due to chronic hypertension.
